capture_method: Playwright (chromium, headless) via local static server (python -m http.server) on the SOURCE_SHA working tree. No CSS was injected to hide the sticky header for any image in this set.
full_page_capture_method: For sp_full_*/tablet_full_*/pc_full_* only: page.screenshot(full_page=True) was taken once per screen size to render the ENTIRE page (Chromium's native full-page capture, which renders the whole DOM height in a single pass), then the resulting image was sliced with PIL into equal-height, contiguous, non-overlapping horizontal bands (previous round's mistake was scrolling to only 4-6 fixed viewport positions, which left gaps between chunks and cut off the page before the footer; this round slices one complete image so there is no gap by construction). Each chunk's exact pixel y_start/y_end is recorded below and in _capture_ranges.json alongside this manifest.
detail_crop_method: For sp_faq_list_with_2_3_5_opened / sp_net_option_honestbox / sp_calc_case6_family_home / sp_mainline_procedure_honestbox: the target element's true height was measured after scrolling the page back to scrollY=0 (clicking FAQ accordion buttons had auto-scrolled the page, which previously caused bounding_box() to under-measure the element and made Playwright fall back to an internal multi-scroll capture that showed the sticky header repeating mid-crop). The viewport height was then resized to fit the element's full height before calling element.screenshot(), so the whole element renders in one pass with no internal scrolling and no header artifact. The real sticky header is simply outside the cropped region in these images (not hidden by CSS).
